## 🐺 C2C/🎬 NukeMax/Audio


### NukeMax_AudioDriveMask

**Shown in the menu as:** Audio Drive Mask

Modulate a per-frame mask by an audio-driven float curve via intensity scaling, dilation, or feathering.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/audio/__init__.py`  
**Provenance:** none named (no PORTED FROM header, no CREDITS / NOTICE section names this file)

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mask` | `MASK` |  | Per-frame mask batch to modulate. |
| `curve` | `FLOAT` |  | Per-frame float curve (e.g. from Audio To Float Curve). |
| `mode` | choice: `intensity`, `dilate`, `feather` |  | How the curve modulates the mask: brightness, morphological dilation, or Gaussian feather. |
| `amount` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…32.0 | Strength of the modulation. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `mask` | `MASK` | Mask modulated frame-by-frame by the curve. |


---

### NukeMax_AudioDriveSchedule

**Shown in the menu as:** Audio Drive Schedule

Map an audio float curve to a per-frame value schedule (e.g. CFG/denoise) and emit it as JSON plus the scaled curve.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/audio/__init__.py`  
**Provenance:** none named (no PORTED FROM header, no CREDITS / NOTICE section names this file)

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `curve` | `FLOAT` |  | Per-frame float curve to remap. |
| `min_value` | `FLOAT` | default `4.0`, range 0.0…100.0 | Schedule value when the curve is at 0. |
| `max_value` | `FLOAT` | default `12.0`, range 0.0…100.0 | Schedule value when the curve is at 1. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `schedule_json` | `STRING` | JSON-encoded list of per-frame schedule values. |
| 1 | `curve` | `FLOAT` | Per-frame schedule values as a float list. |


---

### NukeMax_AudioLoadAnalyze

**Shown in the menu as:** Audio Load & Analyze

Load an audio file and compute STFT magnitude, onset envelope, BPM, spectral centroid and RMS as AUDIO_FEATURES.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/audio/__init__.py`  
**Provenance:** none named (no PORTED FROM header, no CREDITS / NOTICE section names this file)

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `STRING` | default `""` | Filesystem path to the audio file (wav/flac/mp3 if librosa is available). |
| `n_fft` | `INT` | default `2048`, range 256…16384 | FFT window size used for the STFT. |
| `hop_length` | `INT` | default `512`, range 64…4096 | STFT hop length in samples. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `audio` | `AUDIO_FEATURES` | Bundle of audio features (waveform, STFT, onsets, centroid, RMS). |
| 1 | `bpm` | `FLOAT` | Estimated tempo in beats per minute. |
| 2 | `info` | `STRING` | Human-readable summary string. |


---

| `log_scale` | `BOOLEAN` | default `True` | If true, display log10 magnitude; otherwise linear magnitude. |

### NukeMax_AudioToFloatCurve

**Shown in the menu as:** Audio → Float Curve

Convert an audio feature band (bass/mid/treble/onsets/centroid/full) into a per-frame float curve and 1D viz mask.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/audio/__init__.py`  
**Provenance:** none named (no PORTED FROM header, no CREDITS / NOTICE section names this file)

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio` | `AUDIO_FEATURES` |  | Audio feature bundle from Audio Load & Analyze. |
| `frame_count` | `INT` | default `60`, range 1…100000 | Length of the output curve in frames. |
| `fps` | `FLOAT` | default `30.0`, range 1.0…240.0 | Target frames-per-second for time-aligning the curve. |
| `band` | choice: `full`, `bass`, `mid`, `treble`, `onsets`, `centroid` |  | Which audio feature band to extract the curve from. |
| `smoothing` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Temporal Gaussian smoothing of the curve (0=none). |
| `gain` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…32.0 | Multiplier applied to the curve before clamping. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `curve` | `FLOAT` | Per-frame float curve normalized to [0,1]. |
| 1 | `curve_image_1d` | `MASK` | 1D mask visualization of the curve over time. |

## 🐺 C2C/🎬 NukeMax/Channel


### NukeMax_Copy

**Shown in the menu as:** Copy (NukeMax)

Nuke Copy: build an output from B's format by routing each of R/G/B/A from either input. The default copies A's alpha onto B's RGB — the standard 'attach this matte to that plate' move. Values pass through unchanged, so an HDR plate stays HDR.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/nuke_merge.py`  
**Provenance:** none named (no PORTED FROM header, no CREDITS / NOTICE section names this file)

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A` | `IMAGE` |  | Source of the copied channels. |
| `B` | `IMAGE` |  | Background. The output takes B's resolution. |
| `out_R` | choice: `B.R`, `B.G`, `B.B`, `B.A`, `B.Lum`, `A.R`, `A.G`, `A.B`, … (+4) | default `"B.R"` | — |
| `out_G` | choice: `B.R`, `B.G`, `B.B`, `B.A`, `B.Lum`, `A.R`, `A.G`, `A.B`, … (+4) | default `"B.G"` | — |
| `out_B` | choice: `B.R`, `B.G`, `B.B`, `B.A`, `B.Lum`, `A.R`, `A.G`, `A.B`, … (+4) | default `"B.B"` | — |
| `out_A` | choice: `B.R`, `B.G`, `B.B`, `B.A`, `B.Lum`, `A.R`, `A.G`, `A.B`, … (+4) | default `"A.A"` | — |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | — |
| 1 | `alpha` | `MASK` | — |

### NukeMax_CameraGamutConvert

**Shown in the menu as:** Camera Gamut Convert

Convert scene-linear RGB between gamuts (ARRI Wide Gamut 3/4, Sony S-Gamut3(.Cine), Panasonic V-Gamut, Canon Cinema Gamut, RED Wide Gamut RGB, DaVinci Wide Gamut, Blackmagic Gen5, ACES AP0/AP1, Rec.709, Rec.2020, P3, AdobeRGB). Matrices are derived at import from the vendors' published chromaticities with the adaptation OCIO's ACES configs use (CAT02 for camera gamuts, Bradford otherwise) — not copied from a reference pack. Input must already be LINEAR: decode the log curve first. Negatives and values above 1.0 are preserved; out-of-gamut colour is reported, not clipped.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/ocio_color/__init__.py`  
**Provenance:** ComfyUI-OCIO — Slava Sexton (AI VFX NEWS) (https://github.com/SlavaSexton/ComfyUI-OCIO) - per CREDITS.md

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | Scene-LINEAR image. Decode any log curve first. |
| `from_gamut` | choice: `ACES 2065-1 (AP0)`, `ACEScg (AP1)`, `sRGB / Rec.709`, `Rec.2020`, `P3-D65`, `DCI-P3`, `AdobeRGB`, `ARRI Wide Gamut 3`, … (+9) | default `"ARRI Wide Gamut 3"` | — |
| `to_gamut` | choice: `ACES 2065-1 (AP0)`, `ACEScg (AP1)`, `sRGB / Rec.709`, `Rec.2020`, `P3-D65`, `DCI-P3`, `AdobeRGB`, `ARRI Wide Gamut 3`, … (+9) | default `"ACEScg (AP1)"` | — |
| `mix` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | Image in the destination gamut. |
| 1 | `info` | `STRING` | The 3x3 matrix used, its published source, and the fraction of pixels that landed out of gamut (negative) in the destination. |

### NukeMax_ColorLookup

**Shown in the menu as:** ColorLookup (NukeMax)

Nuke ColorLookup: a master lookup curve followed by per-channel R/G/B/A curves. Piecewise-linear between control points and linearly extrapolated beyond them, so HDR values above 1.0 are remapped rather than clipped.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/nuke_grade.py`

| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | — |
| `master` | `STRING` | default `"0,0; 1,1"` | Control points as 'x,y' pairs separated by ';'. The curve is linearly extrapolated past the first and last point, so values above 1.0 keep moving instead of flattening into a clamp. |
| `red` | `STRING` | default `"0,0; 1,1"` | Control points as 'x,y' pairs separated by ';'. The curve is linearly extrapolated past the first and last point, so values above 1.0 keep moving instead of flattening into a clamp. |
| `green` | `STRING` | default `"0,0; 1,1"` | Control points as 'x,y' pairs separated by ';'. The curve is linearly extrapolated past the first and last point, so values above 1.0 keep moving instead of flattening into a clamp. |
| `blue` | `STRING` | default `"0,0; 1,1"` | Control points as 'x,y' pairs separated by ';'. The curve is linearly extrapolated past the first and last point, so values above 1.0 keep moving instead of flattening into a clamp. |
| `alpha` | `STRING` | default `"0,0; 1,1"` | Control points as 'x,y' pairs separated by ';'. The curve is linearly extrapolated past the first and last point, so values above 1.0 keep moving instead of flattening into a clamp. |
| `mix` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Dissolve the result back toward the input. |

### NukeMax_Grade

**Shown in the menu as:** Grade (NukeMax)

Nuke Grade: blackpoint/whitepoint remap to lift/gain, multiply, offset and gamma, exactly as Nuke computes it: A = multiply*(gain-lift)/(whitepoint-blackpoint), B = offset+lift-A*blackpoint, out = (A*in+B)^(1/gamma) (gamma leaves values <= 0 alone). black_clamp (on) / white_clamp (off) as in Nuke; reverse undoes the grade; mix blends with the input. Linear float: no other clamp.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/essentials/__init__.py`  
**Provenance:** none named (no PORTED FROM header, no CREDITS / NOTICE section names this file)

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | — |
| `blackpoint` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -1.0…1.0, step 0.001 | — |
| `whitepoint` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…4.0, step 0.001 | — |
| `lift` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -1.0…1.0, step 0.001 | — |
| `gain` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…4.0, step 0.001 | — |
| `multiply` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…8.0, step 0.001 | — |
| `offset` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -1.0…1.0, step 0.001 | — |
| `gamma` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.01…5.0, step 0.01 | — |

**Optional inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mask` | `MASK` |  | Where the grade applies; another size is resized to the image. |
| `black_clamp` | `BOOLEAN` | default `True` | Clamp negative results to 0 (Nuke's default). |
| `white_clamp` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Clamp results above 1 (off: highlights stay, linear float). |
| `reverse` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Apply the inverse grade - undoes this grade with the same settings. |
| `mix` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Blend with the input (0 = untouched). |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | — |

### NukeMax_HueCorrect

**Shown in the menu as:** HueCorrect (NukeMax)

Nuke HueCorrect: six hue buckets (red/yellow/green/cyan/blue/magenta) each drive a gain on either saturation or luminance. Weights are triangular with 60-degree spacing, so leaving every gain at 1.0 is an exact identity. Hue is measured scale-invariantly, so HDR pixels are bucketed correctly instead of all reading as white.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/nuke_grade.py`  
**Provenance:** none named (no PORTED FROM header, no CREDITS / NOTICE section names this file)

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | — |
| `target` | choice: `saturation`, `luminance` | default `"saturation"` | saturation = chroma gain about Rec.709 luma; luminance = overall gain on that hue. |
| `red` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…4.0, step 0.01 | — |

### NukeMax_LUTApply

**Shown in the menu as:** LUT Apply (.cube)

Apply an Iridas/Adobe .cube LUT (1D or 3D) with tetrahedral or trilinear interpolation. A LUT is only defined over its domain (normally 0-1); rather than silently crushing every highlight to the LUT's white corner, this node lets you extrapolate along the LUT's own edge gradient (default), clamp (Nuke Vectorfield behaviour), or pass out-of-domain pixels through. The fraction of samples that fell outside the domain is always reported in `info`.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/ocio_color/__init__.py`  
**Provenance:** ComfyUI-OCIO — Slava Sexton (AI VFX NEWS) (https://github.com/SlavaSexton/ComfyUI-OCIO) - per CREDITS.md

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | — |
| `lut_file` | choice: `(no LUT files found — see tooltip)` |  | A .cube file from ComfyUI/models/luts/ or the input folder. |
| `interpolation` | choice: `tetrahedral`, `trilinear` | default `"tetrahedral"` | Tetrahedral matches Nuke/Resolve and is more accurate on the neutral axis. Trilinear is the cheaper classic. |
| `above_domain` | choice: `extrapolate`, `clamp`, `passthrough` | default `"extrapolate"` | extrapolate = continue along the LUT's edge gradient (HDR survives). clamp = Nuke Vectorfield behaviour, crushes highlights. passthrough = out-of-domain pixels keep their input value. |
| `mix` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass. |

**Optional inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `native_lut_path` | `STRING` | default `""` | When set, load .3dl/.csp/.spi* from this path instead of lut_file. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | Image with the LUT applied. |
| 1 | `info` | `STRING` | LUT title, size, domain, interpolation, and the fraction of samples outside the LUT domain. |

| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | — |
| `lift_r` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -1.0…1.0, step 0.001 | Shadow lift: raises the black point without moving white. 0 = no-op. |
| `lift_g` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -1.0…1.0, step 0.001 | Shadow lift: raises the black point without moving white. 0 = no-op. |
| `lift_b` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -1.0…1.0, step 0.001 | Shadow lift: raises the black point without moving white. 0 = no-op. |
| `gamma_r` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.01…4.0, step 0.001 | Gamma (sign-preserving power, exponent 1/gamma). 1 = no-op; >1 brightens midtones. |
| `gamma_g` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.01…4.0, step 0.001 | Gamma (sign-preserving power, exponent 1/gamma). 1 = no-op; >1 brightens midtones. |
| `gamma_b` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.01…4.0, step 0.001 | Gamma (sign-preserving power, exponent 1/gamma). 1 = no-op; >1 brightens midtones. |
| `gain_r` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…4.0, step 0.001 | Gain: multiplies the channel. 1 = no-op. |
| `gain_g` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…4.0, step 0.001 | Gain: multiplies the channel. 1 = no-op. |
| `gain_b` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…4.0, step 0.001 | Gain: multiplies the channel. 1 = no-op. |
| `offset_r` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -1.0…1.0, step 0.001 | Offset: adds a constant to the channel. 0 = no-op. |
| `offset_g` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -1.0…1.0, step 0.001 | Offset: adds a constant to the channel. 0 = no-op. |
| `offset_b` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -1.0…1.0, step 0.001 | Offset: adds a constant to the channel. 0 = no-op. |
| `contrast` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.01…4.0, step 0.001 | Contrast about pivot (sign-preserving power). 1 = no-op. |
| `pivot` | `FLOAT` | default `0.18`, range -1.0…4.0, step 0.001 | Contrast pivot point. Default 0.18 = scene-linear mid-gray (18% reflectance). |
| `saturation` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…4.0, step 0.001 | Saturation, luminance-preserving (Rec.709 luma weights). 1 = no-op, 0 = grayscale. |
| `mix` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass. |
| `clamp_output` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Clamp the graded RGB to 0..1. Default off: values above 1.0 or below 0.0 (scene-linear HDR, out-of-gamut) pass through unclipped. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | Image with the lift/gamma/gain/offset grade applied. |
| 1 | `grade_info` | `STRING` | JSON grade_info describing this grade - wire into OCIO Apply Grade to stamp the same grade elsewhere. |

**Shown in the menu as:** OCIO LookTransform (Nuke)

Apply a creative look defined by the OCIO config (e.g. 'ACES 1.3 Reference Gamut Compression'), converting from an input to an output colourspace. Forward or inverse. Raises if the look, or either colourspace, is not in the config.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/ocio_color/__init__.py`  
**Provenance:** ComfyUI-OCIO — Slava Sexton (AI VFX NEWS) (https://github.com/SlavaSexton/ComfyUI-OCIO) - per CREDITS.md

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | — |
| `config` | choice: `builtin: ACES Studio (LogC3/C4, camera spaces)`, `builtin: ACES CG`, `builtin: OCIO default (ACES)` |  | — |
| `in_colorspace` | `STRING` | default `"ACEScg"` | — |
| `out_colorspace` | `STRING` | default `"ACEScg"` | — |
| `look` | `STRING` | default `""` | Look name from the config. Blank = no look (a plain colourspace conversion). Run 'OCIO Config Info' to list the looks this config defines. |
| `direction` | choice: `forward`, `inverse` | default `"forward"` | — |
| `mix` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Blend with the original: 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = bypass. |

**Optional inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ocio_config` | `NUKEMAX_OCIO_CONFIG` |  | From NukeMax OCIO Config Manager; overrides config. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | — |
| 1 | `info` | `STRING` | — |

### NukeMax_SoftClip

**Shown in the menu as:** SoftClip (NukeMax)

Nuke SoftClip: roll highlights off asymptotically toward a ceiling instead of clipping them flat. Below 'knee' the image is untouched and the slope is continuous at the knee, so no visible edge appears. Optionally does the same on the shadow side.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/nuke_grade.py`  
**Provenance:** none named (no PORTED FROM header, no CREDITS / NOTICE section names this file)

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | — |
| `knee` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range -10.0…100.0, step 0.01 | Values below this are passed through unchanged. |
| `ceiling` | `FLOAT` | default `4.0`, range -10.0…1000.0, step 0.1 | Asymptote. Output approaches but never reaches it. Must be greater than 'knee'. |
| `roll_shadows` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Mirror the rolloff below 'shadow_knee'. |
| `shadow_knee` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -100.0…10.0, step 0.01 | — |
| `floor` | `FLOAT` | default `-1.0`, range -1000.0…10.0, step 0.1 | Lower asymptote. Must be less than 'shadow_knee'. |
| `mix` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | — |

**Optional inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mask` | `MASK` |  | — |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | — |

### NukeMax_MotionBlur

**Shown in the menu as:** MotionBlur (NukeMax)

Motion blur by accumulated resampling: linear (angle + distance in pixels), rotational (degrees about a centre) or zoom (scale about a centre). Samples are averaged in linear float, so a blurred specular keeps its energy instead of being clipped to white.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/nuke_transform.py`  
**Provenance:** none named (no PORTED FROM header, no CREDITS / NOTICE section names this file)

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | — |
| `type` | choice: `linear`, `rotational`, `zoom` | default `"linear"` | — |
| `distance` | `FLOAT` | default `20.0`, range -4096.0…4096.0, step 0.5 | linear: travel in pixels. |
| `angle` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -360.0…360.0, step 0.5 | linear: direction of travel in degrees. |
| `rotation` | `FLOAT` | default `10.0`, range -360.0…360.0, step 0.1 | rotational: total sweep in degrees. |
| `zoom_amount` | `FLOAT` | default `0.1`, range -4.0…4.0, step 0.005 | zoom: total scale change (0.1 = 10%). |
| `samples` | `INT` | default `16`, range 2…128 | More samples = smoother trail, linear cost. |
| `shutter` | choice: `centred`, `leading`, `trailing` | default `"centred"` | — |
| `center_x` | `FLOAT` | default `0.5`, range -2.0…3.0, step 0.005 | — |
| `center_y` | `FLOAT` | default `0.5`, range -2.0…3.0, step 0.005 | — |
| `filter` | choice: `bilinear`, `nearest`, `bicubic` | default `"bilinear"` | — |
| `edges` | choice: `black`, `edge`, `reflection` | default `"edge"` | — |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | — |

## 🐺 C2C/🎬 NukeMax/HDR


### NukeMax_GeneratedHDRDecode

**Shown in the menu as:** Generated HDR Decode (log → linear)

Decode a model's [0,1] output as a log encoding to get scene-linear HDR - and check that the claim holds. Every log curve maps linear zero to a positive code value, so an image with pixels below that point is not in that encoding: those pixels decode to negative light. The check is arithmetic, not a guess, and it catches the case that otherwise passes silently - an sRGB-trained model whose output looks like HDR after decoding but has no highlight detail to recover.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/hdr/generated_hdr.py`  
**Provenance:** radiance — FXTD Studios (https://github.com/fxtdstudios/radiance) - per CREDITS.md

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | A model's [0,1] output, believed to be log-encoded. |
| `log_curve` | choice: `ARRI LogC3`, `ARRI LogC4`, `ACEScct`, `Sony S-Log3`, `RED Log3G10`, `Panasonic V-Log`, `Canon Log 3`, `Cineon` | default `"ARRI LogC3"` | The encoding the model was TRAINED to emit - not one picked for the look. LogC3 carries about 55x linear, LogC4 about 470x, ACEScct about 223x. |

**Optional inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `assume_encoded` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Decode even when the check says the input is not in this encoding. The result is an expansion, not a reconstruction - useful for looking at, not for shipping as HDR. |
| `clamp_negative` | `BOOLEAN` | default `True` | Clamp negative linear values to zero. Turn it OFF only to inspect how far below zero a bad decode goes; an EXR with negative light in it will upset anything downstream. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `hdr_linear` | `IMAGE` | Scene-linear HDR. Values run well above 1.0 - send it to an EXR writer, not to a preview. |
| 1 | `preview` | `IMAGE` | Reinhard-tonemapped for looking at. Scene-linear cannot be shown directly, and a plain clamp would hide the highlights this is about. |
| 2 | `is_encoded` | `BOOLEAN` | False when the input is not actually in the chosen encoding. |
| 3 | `peak_linear` | `FLOAT` | The largest linear value produced. |
| 4 | `report` | `STRING` | What was decoded and whether it meant anything. |

| `use_oiio_writer` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | When off (default), legacy OpenEXR writer. When on, OIIO writes multi-format. |
| `oiio_bit_depth` | choice: `16f`, `32f`, `16`, `8` | default `"16f"` | — |
| `oiio_compression` | `STRING` | default `"zip"` | — |
| `passes` | `NUKE_PASSES` |  | Optional multi-pass bundle; used only with use_oiio_writer. Each frame gets the image's own frame as its R G B A layer plus the passes: per-frame passes ([frames, H, W, C]) by frame, a single-frame bundle on every frame. |
| `ocio_input_colorspace` | `STRING` | default `""` | Working colorspace before write. Empty = no conversion (legacy). |
| `ocio_output_colorspace` | `STRING` | default `""` | File colorspace to encode. Empty = no conversion. |
| `colorspace_in_filename` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Append a short colorspace tag to the output filename (OCIO Write style). |
| `file_path` | `STRING` | default `""` | One path instead of output_dir + filename: a single frame is written to exactly this file, a batch as _0001, _0002... OpenImageIO first; writes metadata_json and aov_alpha. Codecs: ZIPS, ZIP, PIZ, DWAA, DWAB, RLE, None. |
| `metadata_json` | `STRING` | default `""`, multiline | With file_path: a JSON object of EXR attributes to embed, e.g. {"comment": "shot_0010", "camera": "ARRI"}. |
| `aov_alpha` | `MASK` |  | With file_path: a MASK written as a named A channel next to RGB. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | — |
| 1 | `last_path` | `STRING` | — |
| 2 | `info_json` | `STRING` | — |

### NukeMax_OCIORead

**Shown in the menu as:** NukeMax OCIO Read

Reads stills, sequences and video into the OCIO working space: the source space from you, the file's header or the config's file rules (said which), converted to scene_linear or your working space; alpha kept; a native VIDEO of the source clip with its sound.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/io/ocio_rw.py`  
**Provenance:** ComfyUI-ACES-IO — BISAM20 (https://github.com/BISAM20/ComfyUI-ACES-IO) - per CREDITS.md

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | choice: `example.png` |  | A still, a frame of a sequence or a video in the input folder (Upload media adds files; several frames at once = a sequence). |
| `source` | choice: `input folder`, `server path` | default `"input folder"` | — |
| `mode` | choice: `auto`, `single frame`, `sequence`, `video` | default `"auto"` | auto: a numbered frame reads its whole sequence, a video its frames; single frame: only that file. |
| `frame_range` | `STRING` | default `""` | e.g. 1001-1100 or 1001-1100x2 (frame numbers; a video counts from 0, as Load Video (C2C) does). Empty = everything. |
| `missing_frames` | choice: `error`, `black`, `hold`, `nearest`, `skip` | default `"error"` | A gap in the sequence: refuse, black, hold the last frame, the nearest frame, or skip it. |
| `outside_range` | choice: `hold`, `black`, `loop`, `bounce`, `error` | default `"hold"` | A range that reaches past the first / last frame. |
| `frame_shift` | `INT` | default `0`, range -9999999…9999999 | Added to every frame number in frame_numbers and the metadata (a slip, as in Nuke). |

**Optional inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `server_path` | `STRING` | default `""` | — |
| `layer` | `STRING` | default `"auto"` | EXR: the layer for the image (pass_names / passes give the others). |
| `sequence_fps` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range 0.0…1000.0, step 0.001 | A sequence's rate; 0 = the file's own (EXR / DPX) or 24. |
| `ocio_config` | `NUKEMAX_OCIO_CONFIG` |  | From NukeMax OCIO Config Manager; empty = $OCIO, else the built-in ACES studio config. |
| `source_space` | `STRING` | default `""` | Empty = the file's header, else the config's file rules. |
| `working_space` | `STRING` | default `""` | Empty = the config's scene_linear role. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | — |
| 1 | `alpha` | `MASK` | — |
| 2 | `passes` | `C2C_EXR_PASSES` | — |
| 3 | `audio` | `AUDIO` | — |
| 4 | `video` | `VIDEO` | — |
| 5 | `metadata` | `STRING` | — |
| 6 | `frame_numbers` | `STRING` | — |
| 7 | `frame_count` | `INT` | — |
| 8 | `fps` | `FLOAT` | — |

| `output_dir` | `STRING` | default `"nukemax_exr"` | A folder inside ComfyUI's output folder, or an absolute path (a server reachable from other machines: only inside the C2C media roots). |
| `filename` | `STRING` | default `"shot"` | — |
| `frame_pattern` | choice: `name.####.exr`, `name_####.exr` | default `"name.####.exr"` | — |
| `frame_start` | `INT` | default `1001`, range -999999…9999999 | — |
| `padding` | `INT` | default `4`, range 1…10 | — |
| `bit_depth` | choice: `half (16-bit float)`, `float (32-bit)` | default `"half (16-bit float)"` | — |
| `compression` | choice: `zip`, `zips`, `piz`, `pxr24`, `b44`, `b44a`, `dwaa`, `dwab`, … (+2) | default `"zip"` | — |
| `layout` | choice: `single part (layers as channels)`, `multipart (one part per layer)` | default `"single part (layers as channels)"` | — |
| `versioning` | choice: `new version folder (name_v###)`, `none (plain names)` | default `"new version folder (name_v###)"` | A new name_v### folder per write (never touches an earlier one), or plain names in output_dir. |
| `overwrite` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Replace files that already exist. Off: a write that would replace a file is refused, naming it. |
| `sidecar` | `BOOLEAN` | default `True` | Also write the manifest as <name>.manifest.json. |

**Optional inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alpha` | `MASK` |  | — |
| `passes` | `C2C_EXR_PASSES` |  | The pass bundle of NukeMax Read EXR Pro / EXR Pass Reader. |
| `metadata` | `STRING` |  | Read EXR Pro / Metadata Reader Pro metadata: its source header is embedded, its fps used. |
| `frame_numbers` | `STRING` | default `""` | Frame mapping, e.g. 1001-1010, 1020 or 1001-1019x2 (one number per image). Empty: count from frame_start. |
| `version` | `INT` | default `0`, range 0…9999 | 0 = the next free version; a number = exactly that version (refused if it exists, unless overwrite). |
| `passes_to_write` | `STRING` | default `""` | Comma-separated pass names; empty = every pass in the bundle. |
| `data_passes_float` | `BOOLEAN` | default `True` | Depth, position, normal, motion and other data passes stay 32-bit float when the beauty is half. |
| `alpha_mode` | choice: `write as given`, `premultiply RGB by alpha` | default `"write as given"` | EXR stores premultiplied (associated) alpha: premultiply a straight image here. |
| `colour_space` | `STRING` | default `""` | The colour space of the written pixels, stored in the header (e.g. ACEScg). Empty = none stored. |
| `convert_from` | `STRING` | default `""` | OCIO: convert the colour channels from this space to colour_space before writing (data passes never). Empty = no conversion. |
| `ocio_config` | `STRING` | default `""` | OCIO config file; empty = $OCIO, else the built-in studio config. |
| `fps` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range 0.0…1000.0, step 0.001 | Written as FramesPerSecond; 0 = the metadata's rate, else none. |
| `embed_metadata` | choice: `source header + writer keys`, `writer keys only` | default `"source header + writer keys"` | — |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `manifest` | `STRING` | — |
| 1 | `written_paths` | `STRING` | — |
| 2 | `frame_count` | `INT` | — |
| 3 | `backend` | `STRING` | — |
| 4 | `metadata_report` | `STRING` | — |

### NukeMax_ChromaKeyer

**Shown in the menu as:** Chroma Keyer (NukeMax)

Screen-colour difference keyer with softness and despill. Outputs the despilled image plus an alpha matte (foreground = 1).

| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | Footage shot against a coloured screen. |

| `tolerance` | `FLOAT` | default `0.05`, range -1.0…1.0, step 0.005 | Where the matte starts to open. Lower = keys more of the screen. |
| `softness` | `FLOAT` | default `0.2`, range 0.001…1.0, step 0.005 | Width of the soft edge between full foreground and full screen. |

| 1 | `matte` | `MASK` | Alpha matte: 1 on the foreground subject, 0 on the screen. |

### NukeMax_HueKeyer

**Shown in the menu as:** HueKeyer (NukeMax)

Pull a matte from a hue range with a saturation floor — the fast way to isolate 'everything green' or 'that red jacket' without a screen. Hue and saturation are both measured scale-invariantly, so an HDR pixel at 8.0 keys the same as the identical colour at 0.8.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/nuke_merge.py`  
**Provenance:** none named (no PORTED FROM header, no CREDITS / NOTICE section names this file)

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | — |
| `hue_center` | `FLOAT` | default `120.0`, range 0.0…360.0, step 1.0 | 0=red, 60=yellow, 120=green, 180=cyan, 240=blue, 300=magenta. |
| `hue_width` | `FLOAT` | default `40.0`, range 0.0…180.0, step 1.0 | Half-width of the fully-keyed band, in degrees. |
| `hue_softness` | `FLOAT` | default `20.0`, range 0.0…180.0, step 1.0 | Degrees of falloff outside the band. |
| `min_saturation` | `FLOAT` | default `0.15`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.005 | Below this, a pixel is too grey to have a reliable hue and is excluded. |
| `saturation_softness` | `FLOAT` | default `0.1`, range 0.001…1.0, step 0.005 | — |
| `invert` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | — |
| `set_alpha` | `BOOLEAN` | default `True` | Write the matte into the output image's alpha channel. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | — |
| 1 | `matte` | `MASK` | — |

### NukeMax_STMapApply

**Shown in the menu as:** STMap Apply (Lens Distortion)

Apply a Nuke-style STMap to an IMAGE. The STMap is an RGB image where R=U, G=V in [0,1]. Each output pixel reads from the source at (R,G). Use this to apply lens distortion / un-distortion.

| `stmap` | `IMAGE` |  | STMap. R=U, G=V in [0,1]. Output resolution matches the STMap. |
| `interpolation` | choice: `bilinear`, `bicubic`, `nearest` | default `"bilinear"` | Sampling mode. |
| `padding_mode` | choice: `zeros`, `border`, `reflection` | default `"border"` | Behaviour outside [0,1] UV range. |

**Optional inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preserve_hdr` | `BOOLEAN` | default `True` | Keep float32 unbounded (no clamp). Disable for SDR images. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | Warped IMAGE at the STMap resolution. |

### NukeMax_Merge

**Shown in the menu as:** Merge (NukeMax)

Nuke Merge: A merged with B by the chosen operation (over, under, atop, in, out, mask, stencil, plus, minus, from, multiply, screen, overlay, difference, max, min, average, divide, conjoint / disjoint over, ...). As in Nuke the operation runs on alpha too, the output takes B's format (A is resized to it), and nothing is clamped. 'mix' (times the optional mask) dissolves the result back toward B.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/essentials/__init__.py`  
**Provenance:** none named (no PORTED FROM header, no CREDITS / NOTICE section names this file)

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A` | `IMAGE` |  | — |
| `B` | `IMAGE` |  | — |
| `operation` | choice: `over`, `under`, `atop`, `in`, `out`, `mask`, `stencil`, `plus`, … (+24) | default `"over"` | — |
| `mix` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Blend the merge result back toward B (1 = full merge). |

**Optional inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mask` | `MASK` |  | Optional matte: the mix is applied only where it is white. |
| `invert_mask` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Use the inverse of the mask. |

**Outputs**

| # | Name | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `image` | `IMAGE` | — |

### NukeMax_ReLight2D

**Shown in the menu as:** ReLight 2D (Light Paint)

Creates realistic lighting effects with multiple light sources, colored lights, and 3D lighting simulation with subject occlusion

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/relight/light_paint.py`  
**Provenance:** ComfyUI-ReLight (MIT) by the ComfyUI-ReLight authors

**Required inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | The input image to apply lighting effects to |
| `preset` | choice: `None`, `Soft Window Light`, `Dramatic Side Light`, `Warm Sunset Glow`, `Cool Blue Moonlight`, `Studio Key Light`, `Rim Light (Behind)`, `Spotlight`, … (+1) | default `"None"` | Select a preset or 'None' for custom settings. NOTE: a preset overrides the widgets below - the values shown on the node are ignored for whatever the preset defines. The one exception is 'effect_strength', which scales the preset instead of being replaced by it |
| `num_light_sources` | `INT` | default `1`, range 1…3, step 1 | Number of light sources (1-3). Lights 2 and 3 have their own position, radius and color, but in color-correction mode they reuse Light 1's correction settings |
| `preserve_positioning` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Keep your own light positions and radii when a preset is selected, instead of letting the preset set them |
| `show_debug_info` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Output a debug visualization image (first image of the batch; zone overlays show Light 1, position and radius indicators are drawn for every light) |
| `use_colored_lights` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Use additive colored light instead of color correction? |
| `use_gradient_mode` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Use directional gradient masks instead of radial? |
| `apply_3d_lighting` | `BOOLEAN` | default `True` | Master switch for occlusion. Leave on and use 'light_direction' to choose the behaviour; turning this off forces 'No Occlusion' |
| `light_direction` | choice: `Behind Subject`, `In Front of Subject`, `No Occlusion` | default `"No Occlusion"` | How light interacts with the subject. 'Behind'/'In Front' require a mask |
| `remove_background` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | Composite the lit result back over the untouched original using the mask, so only the subject is relit. Does not remove anything. Ignored for 'Behind Subject' and 'In Front of Subject' |
| `effect_strength` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…5.0, step 0.1 | Overall intensity multiplier for lighting adjustments/colors, gamma included. 0.0 leaves the image untouched. With a preset active this scales the preset's own strength, so 1.0 is the preset as designed. Does not scale rim_amplification or mask_blur - those have their own controls |
| `mask_blur` | `FLOAT` | default `50.0`, range 0.0…200.0, step 1.0 | Blur radius for light mask edges (smoother transitions) |
| `rim_amplification` | `FLOAT` | default `2.0`, range 0.0…10.0, step 0.1 | Intensity boost specifically for rim light component (when 'Behind Subject') |
| `light_position_x` | `FLOAT` | default `0.5`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Light 1: Horizontal position (0=left, 1=right) |
| `light_position_y` | `FLOAT` | default `0.5`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Light 1: Vertical position (0=top, 1=bottom) |
| `inner_circle_radius` | `FLOAT` | default `0.4`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Light 1: Inner radius (strongest effect area) |
| `outer_circle_radius` | `FLOAT` | default `0.7`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Light 1: Outer radius (falloff area) |
| `light_color_r` | `INT` | default `255`, range 0…255, step 1 | Light 1: Red color (if 'Use Colored Lights' is True) |
| `light_color_g` | `INT` | default `255`, range 0…255, step 1 | Light 1: Green color (if 'Use Colored Lights' is True) |
| `light_color_b` | `INT` | default `255`, range 0…255, step 1 | Light 1: Blue color (if 'Use Colored Lights' is True) |
| `light_intensity` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…3.0, step 0.1 | Light 1: Intensity (if 'Use Colored Lights' is True) |
| `inner_brightness` | `FLOAT` | default `10.0`, range -100.0…100.0, step 1.0 | Light 1: Inner area brightness (Color Correction mode) |
| `inner_contrast` | `FLOAT` | default `5.0`, range -100.0…100.0, step 1.0 | Light 1: Inner area contrast (Color Correction mode) |
| `inner_saturation` | `FLOAT` | default `5.0`, range -100.0…100.0, step 1.0 | Light 1: Inner area saturation (Color Correction mode) |
| `inner_temperature` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -100.0…100.0, step 1.0 | Light 1: Inner area temperature (-100=cool, 100=warm) |
| `inner_tint` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -100.0…100.0, step 1.0 | Light 1: Inner area tint (-100=magenta, 100=green) |
| `inner_gamma` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.1…5.0, step 0.05 | Light 1: Inner area gamma. Above 1.0 brightens midtones, below 1.0 darkens them |
| `outer_brightness` | `FLOAT` | default `-10.0`, range -100.0…100.0, step 1.0 | Light 1: Outer area brightness (Color Correction mode) |
| `outer_contrast` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -100.0…100.0, step 1.0 | Light 1: Outer area contrast (Color Correction mode) |
| `outer_saturation` | `FLOAT` | default `-10.0`, range -100.0…100.0, step 1.0 | Light 1: Outer area saturation (Color Correction mode) |
| `outer_temperature` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -100.0…100.0, step 1.0 | Light 1: Outer area temperature |
| `outer_tint` | `FLOAT` | default `0.0`, range -100.0…100.0, step 1.0 | Light 1: Outer area tint |
| `outer_gamma` | `FLOAT` | default `0.91`, range 0.1…5.0, step 0.05 | Light 1: Outer area gamma. Above 1.0 brightens midtones, below 1.0 darkens them |

| `light2_position_x` | `FLOAT` | default `0.8`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Light 2: Horizontal position |
| `light2_position_y` | `FLOAT` | default `0.2`, range 0.0…1.0, step 0.01 | Light 2: Vertical position |

### NukeMax_RotoShapeStack

Composite up to 6 animated ROTO_SHAPE inputs into a single MASK. Per-layer opacity, feather override, invert, and Nuke-style blend op (union/add/max/sub/intersect/min/replace). All layers are rasterized onto the canvas of shape_1 (other shapes are scaled to match).

## 🐺 C2C/🎬 NukeMax/Viewer


### NukeMax_Viewer

**Shown in the menu as:** Viewer (NukeMax)

Preview an IMAGE with Nuke-style channel isolation (R G B A L, M = matte overlay), gain, gamma and an optional mask overlay. An output node: it runs and shows the frame with nothing after it. The IMAGE output carries the viewed result in linear float (alpha kept for rgba); only the preview is clipped for display.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/viewer/__init__.py`

| `gain` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.1…5.0, step 0.1 | — |
| `show_overlay` | `BOOLEAN` | default `False` | — |

### NukeMax_ViewerPro

**Shown in the menu as:** NukeMax Viewer Pro

A professional viewer on the node: fit / 100% / zoom / pan, R G B A luma, exposure in stops, gamma, gain, checkerboard alpha, exact pixel values, timeline with timecode. VIEW ONLY: the output is the input, untouched, unless you press Apply view to output.

**Source:** `ComfyUI-NukeMaxNodes/nukemax/nodes/viewer/viewer_pro.py`  
**Provenance:** none named (no PORTED FROM header, no CREDITS / NOTICE section names this file)

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | `IMAGE` |  | — |

| Parameter | Type | Constraints | What it does |

| `image_b` | `IMAGE` |  | B, for A/B compare (split / wipe, difference, heatmap, blink). |

| `gain` | `FLOAT` | default `1.0`, range 0.0…100.0, step 0.01 | — |
